description: Create .gitignore, initialise git, write AGENTS.md and docs/GROUND_RULES.md with the house rules
steps: FIRST, before anything else (the loop commits with `git add .` at the end of every task): create `.gitignore` at the repo root containing exactly these lines: `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`, `bin/`, `build/`, `firmware/.pio/`, `firmware/build/`, `firmware/include/secrets.h`, `*.bin`, `*.elf`, `*.map`, `.DS_Store`, `*.log`, `state.json`. Then run `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || git init -b main`. Do NOT delete or edit sticks3-ai-usage.md (the old research report); it stays committed as reference.

Context (repeat in your head before every task; the loop starts you with no memory): this repo is `usaged`, a lean AI-usage monitor owned by Felipe (founder, always authorized). Goal: show the two web "Usage" panels — claude.ai Max 20x (session 5h, weekly all-models, weekly Fable) and chatgpt.com Plus (5h, weekly Codex quota) — first in a local web page served by a Go binary on this Mac, later on an M5StickS3. Poller runs every 900 s; clients re-render ONLY when the snapshot content changed (rev/ETag). Stack: Go 1.26.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/go, ZERO external Go dependencies (stdlib only; `~/go/bin/staticcheck` exists for linting). Firmware later: PlatformIO 6.1.19 (`/opt/homebrew/bin/pio`). Repo root: /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. The 61 KB file sticks3-ai-usage.md is an old research report — reference only, never a spec.

House rules (also written in AGENTS.md; violating any of them is a failed task): (1) NEVER edit ~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/*, the macOS Keychain, or any file named `.env` — the builder may create/edit `.env.example` only; the founder fills `.env` himself. (2) NEVER refresh, rotate, export or copy OAuth tokens: the Claude token is READ from the Keychain item "Claude Code-credentials" and the Codex token is READ from ~/.codex/auth.json; on expiry the UI shows a badge ("run claude" / "run codex"), nothing else. Never set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude-code#37512: it deletes the Keychain item). (3) Tests never touch the network or real credentials: every fetcher is exercised through the fixture transport in testdata/fixtures; live calls only behind USAGED_LIVE=1 and only the founder runs them. (4) Before starting any server process, kill previous instances (`pkill -f 'usaged serve' || true`; `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.usaged 2>/dev/null || true`). (5) Never log or print token values; log only lengths/prefixes (7 chars). (6) Device uploads (pio -t upload / espota) require the founder's explicit authorization for that specific upload — builds, tests and monitors never authorize one. (7) Commit only via the loop's own `git add . && git commit` at the end of a task; never push.

Write `AGENTS.md` (≤150 lines) with sections: Purpose (two sentences from the context above), Project tree (to be filled as tasks land; start with `cmd/usaged`, `internal/{config,snapshot,creds,httpx,format,providers,sched,api,web}`, `testdata/fixtures`, `scripts`, `launchd`, `firmware/`), Build/test commands (`make verify`, `go test ./...`, `go run ./cmd/usaged once --fixtures testdata/fixtures`), the seven house rules VERBATIM, the endpoint provenance summary (Claude oauth/usage + Codex wham/usage are unofficial; official Admin/Usage APIs are out of scope; no admin keys), and the loop rules (one task at a time in ledger order; each task ends by running its own Verify steps; `progress.txt` is append-only). description: Define the snapshot v1 types with JSON encoding, ordering and validation
steps: Snapshot v1 (the ONE contract every client uses; keep it under 1 KB): `{"v":1,"seq":<int, +1 only when rev changes>,"rev":"<8 hex>","generated_at":<unix s of the last CHANGE>,"checked_at":<unix s of the last poll attempt>,"next_sec":900,"providers":[{"id":"claude","label":"Claude","plan":"max_20x","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"CLAUDE 5h","pct":19,"txt":"05:09","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788411000},{"k":"7d","label":"CLAUDE 7d","pct":30,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000},{"k":"7d:Fable","label":"FABLE 7d","pct":20,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000}]},{"id":"codex","label":"ChatGPT","plan":"plus","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"GPT 5h","pct":100,"txt":"23:13","tier":"crit","reset_at":1788401621},{"k":"7d","label":"GPT 7d","pct":31,"txt":"Tue","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788969665},{"k":"bal","label":"GPT bal","pct":null,"txt":"$178.10","tier":"ok","reset_at":null}]}]}`. Provider ids in fixed order: claude, codex, openrouter:main, openrouter:fallback, groq. status ∈ ok|stale|auth|error|off; msg is a ≤24-char human hint ("run claude", "run codex", "429 until 21:40", "no key"). rows[].label ≤10 chars, txt ≤11 chars, pct int or null, tier ∈ ok|warn|crit|off (ok <50, warn 50-79, crit ≥80; off when pct null or status not ok/stale). `rev` = first 8 hex chars of sha256 over the canonical JSON array `[[id,status,plan,[[k,pct,txt,tier],…]],…]` (rows in order, no whitespace, pct null encoded as null) — NOTE: checked_at, generated_at, reset_at, msg and label are NOT part of the hash, so a countdown never changes rev, but any status/tier/pct/txt change does.

Implement `internal/snapshot/types.go`: `type Row struct { K, Label string; Pct *int; Txt, Tier string; ResetAt *int64 }`, `type Provider struct { ID, Label, Plan, Status, Msg string; Rows []Row; FetchedAt int64 /* serialised as fetched_at for the web page; NOT part of the hash */ }`, `type Snapshot struct { V int; Seq int64; Rev string; GeneratedAt, CheckedAt int64; NextSec int; Providers []Provider }` with exact json tags from the contract (`v`,`seq`,`rev`,`generated_at`,`checked_at`,`next_sec`,`providers`; rows: `k`,`label`,`pct`,`txt`,`tier`,`reset_at`; provider: `id`,`label`,`plan`,`status`,`msg`,`fetched_at`,`rows`). Pct/ResetAt nil must encode as JSON null (pointer fields, no omitempty). Add `func (s *Snapshot) Validate() error` enforcing: V==1, provider ids unique and in the canonical order `claude, codex, openrouter:main, openrouter:fallback, groq` (missing ids allowed), status/tier enums, label ≤10 and txt ≤11 runes, msg ≤24. Add `Order(ids)` helper that sorts providers into canonical order.

Tests: golden encode/decode round-trip of the example snapshot from the contract (store it as `testdata/snapshots/example.json`, keep it byte-stable with `json.MarshalIndent` two-space); Validate rejects a 12-char label, an unknown tier, duplicate ids; nil pct encodes as `null`.
Verify: `go test ./internal/snapshot -run 'Types|Golden|Validate' -v 2>&1 | grep -c '^--- PASS'` ≥ 4; `make verify` exits 0.

description: Credential reader for the Claude Code Keychain item behind an injectable command runner, with fixture mode
steps: Verified endpoints (live on 2026-09-02 with the founder's real accounts; both are UNOFFICIAL, read-only, single-user): (A) Claude: `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` with headers `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`, `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`, `Accept: application/json`, `User-Agent: claude-code/<version>` (version = first token of `claude --version`, e.g. 2.1.259; fallback `claude-code/2.1.0`). accessToken comes from `security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -a "<username>" -w` whose stdout is JSON `{"claudeAiOauth":{"accessToken":"sk-ant-oat01-…","refreshToken":"…","expiresAt":1788414949703,"refreshTokenExpiresAt":…,"scopes":[…],"subscriptionType":"max","rateLimitTier":"default_claude_max_20x"}}` (expiresAt is epoch MILLISECONDS; Claude Code rotates it roughly every 8 h; if expiresAt <= now do NOT call, report status auth). Rate-limit hygiene: poll at most every 300 s, on 429 honor `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP-date) else cool down 300 s; bursts can lock the account for ~24 h. (B) Codex/ChatGPT: `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` with `Authorization: Bearer <tokens.access_token>`, `ChatGPT-Account-Id: <tokens.account_id>`, `Accept: application/json`, `User-Agent: codex-cli`. Tokens from ~/.codex/auth.json = `{"auth_mode":"chatgpt","OPENAI_API_KEY":null,"tokens":{"id_token":"<jwt>","access_token":"<jwt, 10-day life>","refresh_token":"rt.1.…","account_id":"<uuid>"},"last_refresh":"2026-08-24T22:29:37.208541Z"}`; decode the access_token JWT payload (base64url, second dot-segment) and read `exp` (unix s); if exp <= now → status auth, no call. Windows are identified by `limit_window_seconds` (18000 → "5h", 604800 → "7d"), NEVER by primary/secondary position; `used_percent` is USED (int). Never POST to /wham/rate-limit-reset-credits/consume.

House rules (also written in AGENTS.md; violating any of them is a failed task): (1) NEVER edit ~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/*, the macOS Keychain, or any file named `.env` — the builder may create/edit `.env.example` only; the founder fills `.env` himself. (2) NEVER refresh, rotate, export or copy OAuth tokens: the Claude token is READ from the Keychain item "Claude Code-credentials" and the Codex token is READ from ~/.codex/auth.json; on expiry the UI shows a badge ("run claude" / "run codex"), nothing else. Never set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude-code#37512: it deletes the Keychain item). (3) Tests never touch the network or real credentials: every fetcher is exercised through the fixture transport in testdata/fixtures; live calls only behind USAGED_LIVE=1 and only the founder runs them. (4) Before starting any server process, kill previous instances (`pkill -f 'usaged serve' || true`; `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.usaged 2>/dev/null || true`). (5) Never log or print token values; log only lengths/prefixes (7 chars). (6) Device uploads (pio -t upload / espota) require the founder's explicit authorization for that specific upload — builds, tests and monitors never authorize one. (7) Commit only via the loop's own `git add . && git commit` at the end of a task; never push.

Implement `internal/format/format.go`: `ResetTxt(reset time.Time, now time.Time, loc *time.Location) string` → if reset is zero → `--`; if reset < now → `now`; if reset − now < 24h → `15:04` in loc; else the 3-letter English weekday of reset in loc (`Mon`); `Tier(pct *int, status string) string` (nil or status not ok/stale → `off`; <50 ok; <80 warn; else crit); `Cents(v float64) int` (round half away from zero); `Money(cents int) string` → `$1.23` (thousands without separators, negative with leading `-`); `Age(now, then int64) string` → `just now`, `12m`, `3h`, `2d`. steps: Snapshot v1 (the ONE contract every client uses; keep it under 1 KB): `{"v":1,"seq":<int, +1 only when rev changes>,"rev":"<8 hex>","generated_at":<unix s of the last CHANGE>,"checked_at":<unix s of the last poll attempt>,"next_sec":900,"providers":[{"id":"claude","label":"Claude","plan":"max_20x","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"CLAUDE 5h","pct":19,"txt":"05:09","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788411000},{"k":"7d","label":"CLAUDE 7d","pct":30,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000},{"k":"7d:Fable","label":"FABLE 7d","pct":20,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000}]},{"id":"codex","label":"ChatGPT","plan":"plus","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"GPT 5h","pct":100,"txt":"23:13","tier":"crit","reset_at":1788401621},{"k":"7d","label":"GPT 7d","pct":31,"txt":"Tue","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788969665},{"k":"bal","label":"GPT bal","pct":null,"txt":"$178.10","tier":"ok","reset_at":null}]}]}`. description: Host test harness for the firmware core: CMake, vendored ArduinoJson single header, framework.h

Proven PlatformIO env (Colibrino, same physical board family): `platform = espressif32@6.12.0`, `board = esp32-s3-devkitc-1` (no m5stack_sticks3 board id exists), `framework = arduino`, `board_build.arduino.partitions = default_8MB.csv`, `board_build.arduino.memory_type = qio_opi`, `build_unflags = -std=gnu++11`, `build_flags = -std=gnu++17 -DESP32S3 -DBOARD_HAS_PSRAM -mfix-esp32-psram-cache-issue -DCORE_DEBUG_LEVEL=1`, `lib_deps = m5stack/M5Unified@0.2.19, m5stack/M5GFX@0.2.26, bblanchon/ArduinoJson@7.4.2`, `monitor_speed = 115200`, `monitor_filters = esp32_exception_decoder`. Do NOT add Colibrino's `-DARDUINO_USB_MODE=0 / -DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0` flags (they exist only for its USB HID mouse and kill the serial console); keep the default USB-JTAG CDC so `pio device monitor` works for the life of the sketch. Arduino core here is 2.0.17 (IDF 4.4): `esp_sleep_enable_ext1_wakeup(mask, mode)` exists, `esp_sleep_enable_ext1_wakeup_io` does NOT. `HTTPClient::setTimeout` takes uint16_t (max 65535 ms). Device is USB-powered and always on in v1: no deep sleep, no OTA, no NTP (the host formats every time string). Architecture (pense-bem convention, founder's habit): `firmware/src/usage/` is pure C++17 with NO Arduino/M5 headers (ArduinoJson single header allowed — it is platform-independent); ONLY `firmware/src/hal/sticks3/*.cpp|*.h` and `firmware/src/main.cpp` may include <M5Unified.h>/<Arduino.h>/<WiFi.h>/<HTTPClient.h>; no `delay()` inside logic; no heap allocation in the per-loop path (bounded char arrays); every stateful piece is an explicit state machine polled with `update(nowMs)`; the renderer diffs (by rev) and pushes. Host tests: `firmware/CMakeLists.txt` builds `firmware/src/usage/*.cpp` + `firmware/test/host/*.cpp` into `firmware/build/usage_tests` with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined`. The physical unit is StickS3 unit #2 (arrived 2026-09-01, never flashed) with hostname `sticks3-usage`; unit #1 (`sticks3-ptt`, MAC AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8) belongs to other projects and must never be targeted. HARD RULE: any upload to a device needs the founder's explicit authorization for that upload; builder tasks are build-only with a UAT block.

Vendor ArduinoJson as ONE header: download `https://github.com/bblanchon/ArduinoJson/releases/download/v7.4.2/ArduinoJson-v7.4.2.h` to `firmware/third_party/ArduinoJson.h` (keep its MIT licence header; add `firmware/third_party/LICENSE-ArduinoJson.txt`). Create `firmware/CMakeLists.txt` (C++17, `include_directories(src third_party test/host)`, `file(GLOB_RECURSE ... src/usage/*.cpp)`, `file(GLOB ... test/host/*.cpp)`, target `usage_tests`, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer`, `add_test`). Create `firmware/test/host/framework.h`: a ~100-line header-only harness modelled on /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/pense-bem-cardputer-adv/test/host/framework.h (read it): `TEST(name)` registration, `ASSERT_TRUE/ASSERT_EQ/ASSERT_STREQ`, a failing assertion throws, `main` prints `PASS <name>` per test and a summary ending in `Failed N`. Add `firmware/test/host/test_smoke.cpp` with one test that parses `{"v":1}` with ArduinoJson on the host (`#define ARDUINOJSON_ENABLE_ARDUINO_STRING 0` etc. as needed) and asserts `doc["v"] == 1`. Add Makefile targets at the repo root: `fw-test` (`cmake -S firmware -B firmware/build && cmake --build firmware/build && ./firmware/build/usage_tests`) and `fw-build` (`cd firmware && pio run`); keep `make verify` Go-only (the fast standing gate) and add `make verify-all` = verify + fw-test + fw-build.

Verify: `make fw-test` exits 0, output contains `PASS smoke` and ends in `Failed 0`; `make fw-build` ends with `SUCCESS`; `grep -c 'ARDUINOJSON_VERSION "7.4.2"' firmware/third_party/ArduinoJson.h` prints 1.

HARD RULE: any upload to a device needs the founder's explicit authorization for that upload; builder tasks are build-only with a UAT block.

Snapshot v1 (the ONE contract every client uses; keep it under 1 KB): `{"v":1,"seq":<int, +1 only when rev changes>,"rev":"<8 hex>","generated_at":<unix s of the last CHANGE>,"checked_at":<unix s of the last poll attempt>,"next_sec":900,"providers":[{"id":"claude","label":"Claude","plan":"max_20x","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"CLAUDE 5h","pct":19,"txt":"05:09","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788411000},{"k":"7d","label":"CLAUDE 7d","pct":30,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000},{"k":"7d:Fable","label":"FABLE 7d","pct":20,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000}]},{"id":"codex","label":"ChatGPT","plan":"plus","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"GPT 5h","pct":100,"txt":"23:13","tier":"crit","reset_at":1788401621},{"k":"7d","label":"GPT 7d","pct":31,"txt":"Tue","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788969665},{"k":"bal","label":"GPT bal","pct":null,"txt":"$178.10","tier":"ok","reset_at":null}]}]}`. Provider ids in fixed order: claude, codex, openrouter:main, openrouter:fallback, groq. status ∈ ok|stale|auth|error|off; msg is a ≤24-char human hint ("run claude", "run codex", "429 until 21:40", "no key"). rows[].label ≤10 chars, txt ≤11 chars, pct int or null, tier ∈ ok|warn|crit|off (ok <50, warn 50-79, crit ≥80; off when pct null or status not ok/stale). `rev` = first 8 hex chars of sha256 over the canonical JSON array `[[id,status,plan,[[k,pct,txt,tier],…]],…]` (rows in order, no whitespace, pct null encoded as null) — NOTE: checked_at, generated_at, reset_at, msg and label are NOT part of the hash, so a countdown never changes rev, but any status/tier/pct/txt change does.

Implement `firmware/src/usage/model.h/.cpp` (namespace `usage`): `struct Row { char k[12]; char label[11]; int16_t pct /* -1 = null */; char txt[12]; uint8_t tier /* 0 ok 1 warn 2 crit 3 off */; }`, `struct Provider { char id[24]; char label[12]; char plan[12]; uint8_t status /* 0 ok 1 stale 2 auth 3 error 4 off */; char msg[25]; uint8_t rowCount; Row rows[6]; }`, `struct Model { uint8_t v; uint32_t seq; char rev[9]; uint32_t generatedAt; uint16_t nextSec; uint8_t providerCount; Provider providers[5]; }`; `bool parseSnapshot(const char* json, size_t len, Model& out, char* err, size_t errLen)` using ArduinoJson (`JsonDocument`; on the host it allocates from the heap, on the device that is fine at fetch time, NOT in the render loop), copying with bounded `snprintf`/`strlcpy`-equivalents (write a local `copyStr`), truncating silently but never overflowing; rejects v != 1, > 5 providers, > 6 rows, missing rev. Copy the Go golden `testdata/snapshots/example.json` and `example_full.json` into `firmware/test/host/fixtures/` as C string literals via a tiny generated header `fixtures.h` (write a `firmware/scripts/gen_fixtures.py` that emits `static const char* kSnapshotExample = R"json(...)json";` and run it; commit the output).

Tests `test_model.cpp`: example parses → 2 providers, claude has 3 rows, `FABLE 7d` pct 20 tier 0, codex row `GPT 5h` pct 100 tier 2, rev is 8 chars, seq matches; example_full → 5 providers in canonical order; malformed JSON → false with a non-empty err; a 12-char label is truncated to 10 without overflow (ASan clean); `v:2` rejected.

Verify: `make fw-test` prints `PASS model_parses_example`, `PASS model_rejects_bad_version` (name the tests so) and ends in `Failed 0`; `make fw-build` still `SUCCESS` (compile the core into the firmware even if unused yet).

description: HAL: always-on non-blocking Wi-Fi with hostname sticks3-usage, reconnect, [NET] lines
steps: Firmware context: target M5StickS3 (ESP32-S3-PICO-1-N8R8: 8 MB flash + 8 MB octal PSRAM; ST7789P3 135×240 LCD → `M5.Display.setRotation(1)` gives 240×135 landscape; BtnA = KEY1 GPIO11, BtnB = KEY2 GPIO12; side PWR button is NOT an app button (double-click = power off, long press = ROM download mode); BMI270 IMU at I2C 0x68, ES8311 codec, M5PM1 PMIC, 250 mAh battery; `M5.getBoard() == m5::board_t::board_M5StickS3` (enum 26). Proven PlatformIO env (Colibrino, same physical board family): `platform = espressif32@6.12.0`, `board = esp32-s3-devkitc-1` (no m5stack_sticks3 board id exists), `framework = arduino`, `board_build.arduino.partitions = default_8MB.csv`, `board_build.arduino.memory_type = qio_opi`, `build_unflags = -std=gnu++11`, `build_flags = -std=gnu++17 -DESP32S3 -DBOARD_HAS_PSRAM -mfix-esp32-psram-cache-issue -DCORE_DEBUG_LEVEL=1`, `lib_deps = m5stack/M5Unified@0.2.19, m5stack/M5GFX@0.2.26, bblanchon/ArduinoJson@7.4.2`, `monitor_speed = 115200`, `monitor_filters = esp32_exception_decoder`. Do NOT add Colibrino's `-DARDUINO_USB_MODE=0 / -DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=0` flags (they exist only for its USB HID mouse and kill the serial console); keep the default USB-JTAG CDC so `pio device monitor` works for the life of the sketch. Arduino core here is 2.0.17 (IDF 4.4): `esp_sleep_enable_ext1_wakeup(mask, mode)` exists, `esp_sleep_enable_ext1_wakeup_io` does NOT. `HTTPClient::setTimeout` takes uint16_t (max 65535 ms). Device is USB-powered and always on in v1: no deep sleep, no OTA, no NTP (the host formats every time string). Architecture (pense-bem convention, founder's habit): `firmware/src/usage/` is pure C++17 with NO Arduino/M5 headers (ArduinoJson single header allowed — it is platform-independent); ONLY `firmware/src/hal/sticks3/*.cpp|*.h` and `firmware/src/main.cpp` may include <M5Unified.h>/<Arduino.h>/<WiFi.h>/<HTTPClient.h>; no `delay()` inside logic; no heap allocation in the per-loop path (bounded char arrays); every stateful piece is an explicit state machine polled with `update(nowMs)`; the renderer diffs (by rev) and pushes. Host tests: `firmware/CMakeLists.txt` builds `firmware/src/usage/*.cpp` + `firmware/test/host/*.cpp` into `firmware/build/usage_tests` with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined`. The physical unit is StickS3 unit #2 (arrived 2026-09-01, never flashed) with hostname `sticks3-usage`; unit #1 (`sticks3-ptt`, MAC AC:27:6E:D2:68:B8) belongs to other projects and must never be targeted. HARD RULE: any upload to a device needs the founder's explicit authorization for that upload; builder tasks are build-only with a UAT block.

Create `firmware/src/hal/sticks3/net.h/.cpp` modelled on Colibrino's always-on variant (read /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/Colibrino/sticks3/src/main.cpp functions `startOtaNetworking` and `updateOta` for the shape, WITHOUT OTA): `void netBegin()` → `WiFi.persistent(false); WiFi.mode(WIFI_STA); WiFi.setHostname("sticks3-usage"); WiFi.setAutoReconnect(true); WiFi.setSleep(true); WiFi.begin(WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASS);` (secrets.h; if `firmware/include/secrets.h` is missing the build must fail with a clear `#error copy include/secrets.h.example to include/secrets.h`); `void netUpdate(uint32_t nowMs)` → tracks state {connecting, connected, lost}, re-issues `WiFi.begin` every 30 s while not connected, emits `[NET]` lines only on state transitions (via serial_proto), exposes `bool netUp()` and `const char* netIp(char* buf, size_t n)`. Draw a tiny wifi dot in the top bar later (screen task). For the builder's compile check, create `firmware/include/secrets.h` ONLY IF ABSENT with placeholder values copied from the example (it is git-ignored) — never overwrite an existing one.

Verify: `make fw-build` ends with `SUCCESS`; `grep -n 'setHostname("sticks3-usage")' firmware/src/hal/sticks3/net.cpp` matches; `git status --short | grep -c secrets.h$` prints 0 (ignored). No upload.

Create `firmware/src/hal/sticks3/fetch.h/.cpp`: `struct FetchResult { int code; char rev[9]; uint32_t ms; String body; /* body only on 200 */ }`; `bool fetchUsage(const char* lastRev, FetchResult& out)`: `HTTPClient http; http.setTimeout(8000); http.setReuse(false);` URL `http://USAGED_HOST:USAGED_PORT/v1/usage`; headers `X-Device-Token: USAGED_DEVICE_TOKEN`, and if lastRev non-empty `If-None-Match: "<lastRev>"`; `const char* keys[] = {"ETag"}; http.collectHeaders(keys, 1);` `int code = http.GET();` on 304: do NOT call getString(); copy the ETag (strip quotes and any `W/`) into out.rev; on 200: `out.body = http.getString()` (≤ 4 KB expected; reject > 8 KB), rev from ETag; other codes/negative: out.code = code (HTTPClient negative codes for timeouts → emit `err=timeout`/`err=conn`); always `http.end()`. Emit the `[FETCH]` line via serial_proto with the elapsed ms. Then in `main.cpp` add the poll state machine: first fetch 3 s after `netUp()` becomes true, then every 300 s (`kPollMs = 300000`), immediately on `BtnB.wasClicked()`, with exponential backoff 30 s → 300 s on consecutive failures, and `ESP.restart()` after 12 consecutive failures (log `[ERR] restart after 12 failures` first). On 200: `parseSnapshot` into the Model, `onSnapshot(view, model)`; on parse error emit `[ERR] parse: <err>`.

Verify: `make fw-build` ends with `SUCCESS`; `grep -c 'If-None-Match' firmware/src/hal/sticks3/fetch.cpp` ≥ 1; `grep -c 'getString' firmware/src/hal/sticks3/fetch.cpp` prints 1 (only on the 200 path). No upload. UAT later: `[FETCH] code=200 …` then `[FETCH] code=304 …` every 5 min while the host snapshot is unchanged.

description: Power behaviour: on battery cut the screen rail and deep sleep; wake on ext1 buttons or a 60s timer (USB-insert ext0 is disabled per ORDER #29 — PM1 GPIO1 IRQ conflicts with SDA); flashed over OTA
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2 (MAC 14:c1:9f:d4:d5:34), hostname sticks3-usage, port /dev/cu.usbmodem101 (location-based, never hardcode). PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 = Arduino core 2.0.17 = ESP-IDF 4.4.7. Purity rule: only firmware/src/hal/sticks3/* and main.cpp may include M5/Arduino headers. Gates: make fw-test (host) and make fw-build. Any device upload needs Felipe explicit authorization; the Solvr room is the audit trail.

Felipe requirement: screen should die if not plugged; device must deep sleep and wake on USB insert or button. USB-present test is M5.Power.getVBUSVoltage() > 4000 mV (measured 4904-5004 docked). Do NOT use isCharging(): on StickS3 it reads PM1 GPIO0 charge-status, so a full battery on USB reports not-charging. M5.Display.sleep() + setBrightness(0) does NOT cut the panel rail; the backlight is ESP32 LEDC PWM on GPIO38. The rail is PM1 GPIO2 (L3B): cut it with M5.Power.M5pm1.setGPIOOutput(m5::M5PM1_Class::gpio2, false) AFTER M5.Display.sleep + waitDisplay; M5GFX re-asserts it on next boot.

ORDER #29: USB-insert ext0 wake via PM1 GPIO1 IRQ is DISABLED — driving PM1 GPIO1 push-pull conflicts with the SDA line and hangs PMIC I2C reads after wake (see docs/DEVICES.md). Wake sources are ext1 buttons only (BtnA GPIO11, BtnB GPIO12, ESP_EXT1_WAKEUP_ANY_LOW with pullup_en + pulldown_dis on each) plus a 60 s timer backstop (not 3600 s) so a USB cable insert is noticed within a minute. The instant-wake guard counter (g_powerGuard, RTC_DATA_ATTR) is kept in main.cpp as monitor-only for the follow-up ext0 experiment; it does not affect the sleep path. VbusDebouncer (ORDER #26) stays in vbusPresent().

Deep-sleep teardown (ptt.ino:191-211, DO NOT THIN): ES8311 codec at 0x18 (0x0D=0xFC, 0x0E=0x6A, 0x00=0x00); BMI270 at 0x68 (0x7D=0x00 then 0x7C=0x03); PM1 GPIO3 (PA off) + GPIO2 (LCD rail off); WiFi.disconnect(true) + WIFI_OFF. powerDecide(vbus, now, graceAnchorMs, graceMs=20000) in the PURE core (renamed from lastActivityMs; caller owns the anchor): on USB always StayAwake; on battery SleepNow when (now - graceAnchorMs) >= graceMs. ORDER #30 grace semantics: grace is NOT active at boot — on wake the caller passes nowMs as graceAnchorMs so powerDecide always returns StayAwake until the first render or fetch failure, so slow Wi-Fi cannot sleep the device before paint. Grace activates on: (a) USB→battery transition (graceAnchor = now, graceActive = true — unplugging is activity), (b) first redraw() completion (graceAnchor = render time), (c) fetch failure (graceAnchor = now). ORDER #31 warm-boot fix: on deep-sleep wake, restore the cached Model from RTC_DATA_ATTR POD but do NOT pre-seed g_view.lastRev (seed only g_lastRev, the HTTP If-None-Match ETag cache, so a 304 still costs no traffic). Set g_view.needsRedraw = true on all wake causes so the cached snapshot is painted exactly once (g_paintedThisBoot flag forces one paint when g_hasModel is true, even if needsRedraw was cleared). Timer wake on battery no longer sleeps immediately — it paints the cached snapshot, then the 60 s timer backstop re-arms only after the grace window expires, so the screen is fresh on every wake cycle.

Verify: host tests for powerDecide + VbusDebouncer (10 host tests PASS incl. 2 new ORDER #30 grace-anchor tests, make fw-test Failed 0) + 1 new ORDER #31 onSnapshot wake-render test in test_render_plan; make fw-build SUCCESS RAM ~16.5% 0 warnings; fresh-clone cmake build+tests green. HARDWARE UAT over OTA (needs Felipe explicit authorization): flash with make fw-ota; Felipe unplugs USB and within ~20 s the screen must go FULLY dark (not merely dim) and stay dark; pressing BtnA must paint the cached screen for ~20 s then go dark again; plugging USB back in must bring the screen back within a couple of seconds WITHOUT any button press, then poll + render once then 304. description: IMU double tap to flip the screen 180 degrees (persisted across reboot/sleep/OTA) + BtnA long-press refresh; shake-to-refresh explicitly dropped
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2, hostname sticks3-usage. PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 / Arduino core 2.0.17 / ESP-IDF 4.4.7, M5Unified 0.2.19 + M5GFX 0.2.28. Purity rule: gesture LOGIC goes in the pure core (firmware/src/usage/, no M5 or Arduino headers, host-tested by 'make fw-test'); only firmware/src/hal/sticks3/* and main.cpp may touch M5. Flash this over OTA ('make fw-ota'), no cable. Any upload needs Felipe's explicit authorization in the Solvr room.

BATCHING (ORDER #34): this is one of FOUR firmware tasks (double-tap flip + version in the top bar, battery percentage, alert banner, pages split by paid vs free) that must be coded and committed separately in ledger order but flashed TOGETHER — do NOT run make fw-ota until all three are committed and green, then flash once and run ONE combined hardware UAT with Felipe. He is the only person who can do the device checks and each flash costs him an interruption.

Felipe's decision (2026-09-04), after living with the device: DOUBLE TAP to flip the screen 180 degrees is a MUST, and so is the battery indicator in the next task. SHAKE TO REFRESH IS DROPPED — his reasoning: on battery the screen is dark almost all the time, so to look at the device you already press a button, and that button both wakes it and refreshes. A shake gesture would be a control nobody reaches for. Do NOT implement shake detection; do not add a shake threshold, a shake test, or a [GESTURE] shake line. Keep BtnA long-press as a second explicit refresh trigger.

Hardware facts already verified for this board, do not re-derive: the IMU is a BMI270 at I2C address 0x68 (NOT 0x69) on SDA GPIO47 / SCL GPIO48; M5Unified probes 0x69 then 0x68 and a hardcoded 0x69 read returns all zeros. The firmware currently sets internal_imu=false in M5.config() — change it to true and confirm M5.Imu.isEnabled(). The BMI270 leaks about 1 mA if left running, so task 40's sleep teardown MUST keep suspending it (0x68: 0x7D=0x00 then 0x7C=0x03); on battery the device sleeps anyway, so the IMU only runs during the short awake windows. Do NOT attempt gesture wake-from-sleep: BMI270 INT1 is wired to the PMIC's GPIO4, not to any ESP32 pin, and cannot wake the SoC — proven on this hardware. Also do NOT touch PM1 GPIO1 or any PM1 IRQ register (BUG 40b: that line conflicts with SDA and hangs the PMIC bus).

Design: implement firmware/src/usage/gesture.{h,cpp} as a PURE state machine with no hardware dependency — `enum class Gesture { none, double_tap }` and `Gesture feed(float ax, float ay, float az, uint32_t nowMs)` fed from a ~50 Hz poll of M5.Imu.getAccelData in the HAL. DOUBLE TAP: two sharp jerk transients (magnitude spike above roughly 2.5 g lasting under 120 ms) separated by 120-500 ms, with a 1 s lockout afterwards, and no firing while the device is being picked up or set down (a slow magnitude ramp must never register). Tune the thresholds from real captures rather than guessing: while the device is cabled, log raw accel magnitude as `[IMU] mag=<f>` behind a build flag, ask Felipe to double-tap the case a few times and to carry it around, pick thresholds that separate the two, and record the captured numbers in docs/DEVICES.md.

Wiring in the HAL and main loop: poll the IMU every 20 ms only while awake and only when no fetch or OTA transfer is in flight; on Gesture::double_tap toggle rotation between 1 and 3 (`M5.Display.setRotation(r)`), persist it with Preferences (namespace "usaged", key "rot") so it survives reboot, deep sleep and OTA, force a full redraw (set needsRedraw and clear g_paintedThisBoot semantics appropriately so the new orientation is painted immediately), and emit `[GESTURE] flip rot=<1|3>`. Load the stored rotation during bring-up BEFORE the first paint so a flipped device never shows one upside-down frame. Add BtnA long press (hold threshold 600 ms, M5.BtnA.wasHold()) as a second force-fetch trigger emitting `[BTN] a_hold refresh`, keeping BtnA short press on page cycling and BtnB short press on refresh. Update firmware/README.md's serial protocol table with `[GESTURE]` and `[BTN]`.

Verify: host tests in firmware/test/host/test_gesture.cpp driving `feed` with synthetic sample sequences — two taps 250 ms apart return exactly one double_tap; two taps 800 ms apart return none; the 1 s lockout suppresses a third tap; steady 1 g gravity in any orientation returns none; a slow 2 g ramp (picking the device up) returns none. `make fw-test` Failed 0 and `make fw-build` SUCCESS with 0 warnings from firmware/src/. HARDWARE UAT over OTA, with Felipe's authorization: after `make fw-ota`, a double tap must flip the screen 180 degrees, the orientation must survive a power cycle AND a sleep/wake cycle, holding BtnA must refresh, and simply carrying or setting the device down must produce no flips at all. Ask Felipe to confirm those four in the room and paste his confirmations into DONE before flipping passes.

description: Settings page: configure everything from the browser, writing the YAML config (phase 2)
steps: Context: usaged (Go, stdlib only, zero external dependencies) at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. House rules in AGENTS.md: never edit .env/.zshrc/settings, never refresh tokens, tests never touch the network, never print key values, read the Solvr room before every task. Felipe: 'like settings page (which tweaks yaml maybe), so user can configure 100% via web (this is a bigger task if you notice). we can do 2 phases.' This is phase 2 — do it only after the layout task above and the YAML config task are both done and passing.

A Settings tab that reads and writes ~/.config/usaged/config.yaml through two new endpoints: GET /v1/config returns the effective config with every secret redacted as set(len=N), and PUT /v1/config accepts the editable subset, validates it, writes the YAML atomically (temp file plus rename, mode 0600) and reloads the scheduler without a restart. description: Settings page is unusable: empty Providers section, unstyled inputs, no plan costs, no key management — make everything configurable from the browser
steps: Context: usaged (Go, stdlib only, zero external dependencies) at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. House rules in AGENTS.md. REMEMBER: internal/web/ is embedded with go:embed, so nothing you change there is visible until 'make build && launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.usaged' — say so in your DONE line.

Felipe's verdict on the settings page shipped in fd97aac: 'settings, HORRIBLE. ideally, one can config EVERYTHING via settings and dont touch configuration, yaml, etc'. His screenshot shows why: the Providers section is COMPLETELY EMPTY (no rows at all), the inputs are unstyled white browser boxes against the dark theme, the poll interval is a raw '900' seconds field, there is no way to set the plan costs the plan-value feature needs, no indication of which API keys are configured, and no feedback after Save. The endpoints work; the page does not. Treat this as a UI task, not a plumbing one.

(a) PROVIDERS SECTION MUST RENDER — this is the headline bug. One card per provider (Claude, ChatGPT, OpenRouter main, OpenRouter fallback, Groq), each with: an enabled toggle, an editable display label, Groq's probe toggle, and for the subscription providers the plan block — cost, currency, optional USD equivalent, plan label — so Felipe can enter his real figures (200 USD Anthropic, 110 BRL ChatGPT) and immediately see the value ratio on the Quota tab. Find why the section renders empty today: GET /v1/config returns the effective config, so either the providers array is absent from the response or the renderer never iterates it. Add a web test asserting the settings markup contains a row per configured provider.

(b) MAKE IT LOOK LIKE THE REST OF THE APP: style inputs, selects, toggles and buttons with the existing dark palette and spacing — no default browser chrome. Replace the raw seconds field with the same 5/10/15/30/60-minute select used in the header, keep them in sync, and label thresholds with their units. Show inline validation on the field that is wrong rather than a silent rejection, and give Save a clear result state — saved, or the specific error — instead of nothing.

(c) API KEYS, the part that resolves Felipe's 'never touch YAML' against the rule that keys must never sit in a config file: store them in the macOS KEYCHAIN, exactly as Claude Code stores its own credential. Each provider card shows the key state (set / not set, and the env var name if one is supplying it) with a 'Set key' action that POSTs the value to a new endpoint which writes it to the Keychain via `security add-generic-password -U -s usaged -a <provider> -w`, and a 'Remove key' action using `security delete-generic-password`. The key is NEVER written to the YAML, NEVER returned by GET /v1/config, and NEVER logged. Resolution order at poll time becomes: environment variable first (so his current .env keeps working), then Keychain. Document the order in README. Expect a one-time macOS permission prompt on first Keychain read, exactly like the Claude credential.

(d) SAFETY, unchanged and non-negotiable: PUT /v1/config still requires the device token even on loopback; every write is preceded by a timestamped backup; an invalid payload changes nothing and names the offending field; a config that would stop the server starting (non-loopback listen with no device token) is refused with an explanation. The key endpoints are token-protected too, accept a value only over loopback, and rate-limit to a few attempts per minute.

Verify: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/config ./internal/web -v` grows by at least 8 (providers render per configured provider; a plan block round-trips; the interval select maps to seconds; an invalid threshold is rejected by field name; the key endpoint writes to and deletes from a FAKE keychain runner injected in tests, never the real one; GET never returns a key; env beats Keychain in the resolution order). `make verify` and `make smoke` exit 0. Then REBUILD AND RESTART the agent and UAT with Felipe: he sets his two plan costs and the interval entirely in the browser, reloads, sees them persist and the value ratio appear on the Quota tab, and confirms the page no longer looks like a raw form.

description: Replace IMU double-tap with BtnB hold-to-flip 180 (the double-tap was impossible: G samples divided by 9.80665) and delete the IMU path; no vibration motor exists on this board
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2, hostname sticks3-usage. PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 / Arduino core 2.0.17 / ESP-IDF 4.4.7, M5Unified 0.2.19 + M5GFX 0.2.28. Purity rule: gesture LOGIC goes in the pure core (firmware/src/usage/, no M5 or Arduino headers, host-tested by 'make fw-test'); only firmware/src/hal/sticks3/* and main.cpp may touch M5. Flash this over OTA ('make fw-ota'), no cable. Any upload needs Felipe's explicit authorization in the Solvr room.

Felipe, replacing his own earlier request after living with it: 'instead of tap, hold either big blue or side button... hold for X secconds, it flips screen 180. easier'. He is right, and it also retires a feature that CANNOT WORK: the IMU double-tap shipped as task 48 divides G-unit samples by 9.80665 (gesture.cpp:20-24) while M5.Imu.getAccelData returns G already (BMI270_Class.cpp:194 aRes = 8.0f/32768.0f over the +/-8 G scale; IMU_Class.cpp:470-484 passes it through untouched), so firing it needs 24.5 G on a sensor that saturates at 8. Do not fix the detector. DELETE it and use the button.

THE BINDING. Read main.cpp:324-350 first: BtnA (GPIO11, the blue centre key) click cycles pages and hold refreshes; BtnB (GPIO12, the big side key) click refreshes; BtnB HOLD is unassigned. That is the one to take. Set BtnB's hold threshold to 1500 ms (board.cpp:25 currently sets 600 for both) so a deliberate hold flips the screen while a normal release still refreshes — BtnB click must keep working exactly as it does now, which is the thing to be careful about, since one threshold governs both. Leave BtnA completely alone: page cycling and hold-to-refresh are unchanged.

ON FLIP: toggle rotation 1 <-> 3, persist to NVS through the existing saveRotation path (that part already works and is not the bug), force a redraw in the new orientation, and emit the existing [GESTURE] flip rot=N serial line so the transcript stays comparable. Because a 1.5 s hold gives no feedback until it fires, show the user something WHILE they hold — a short progress hint or a highlighted footer that appears past about 500 ms and resolves into the flip — so the gesture is discoverable rather than a secret. Nothing that costs a full repaint per frame.

REMOVE THE IMU PATH ENTIRELY, since nothing else uses it: delete src/usage/gesture.{h,cpp} and test/host/test_gesture.cpp, drop imuGestureUpdate and its call at main.cpp:495, drop M5.Imu.begin() at main.cpp:402, set cfg.internal_imu = false in board.cpp:15, and remove the IMU teardown in power.cpp:91 if it becomes dead. This removes a 50 Hz poll from the awake loop and a sensor from the power budget — report the loop-time and any current change in your DONE line. Keep the rotation persistence and the [GESTURE] serial format.

HAPTICS, asked in the same breath — the board HAS NO VIBRATION MOTOR, verified, so do not build one and do not leave the question open. Power_Class.cpp:2132-2168 makes setVibration() a no-op on every board except board_M5StopWatch and board_M5StackCore2. Record that fact in docs/DEVICES.md so it is not re-attempted. The only feedback channels this board has are the ES8311 speaker (internal_spk=false today) and the screen; the hold hint above IS the feedback. DO NOT enable the speaker — that is Felipe's call.

Verify: new host tests for the hold state machine (a release before 1500 ms is a refresh and NOT a flip; a hold past 1500 ms is a flip and NOT a refresh; two holds return to the original rotation; the hint appears only after the hold begins). `make fw-test` Failed 0 with test_gesture.cpp gone, `make fw-build` SUCCESS, and confirm the binary shrank. The real gate is Felipe on the physical device: he holds the side button, the screen flips 180, serial shows [GESTURE] flip rot=3, a short press still refreshes, holding again returns to rot=1, and the orientation survives a reboot. Do not flip this task on host tests alone — green host tests are exactly what hid the double-tap bug.

description: SECURITY: the /v1/keys endpoints are unauthenticated (loopback exemption skips the token) and mutating routes accept cross-site bodies; plus the Groq probe toggle never renders
steps: Context: usaged (Go, stdlib only) at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. House rules in AGENTS.md. internal/web/ is embedded with go:embed — nothing there is visible until 'make build && launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.usaged'.

Two defects found by the planner testing the RUNNING agent after 41a5c9d, not by reading the DONE line. Task 57 is otherwise good: all five providers render, plan costs are there, no key value leaks into GET /v1/config. These two are what it missed.

(a) SECURITY — THE KEY ENDPOINTS ARE UNAUTHENTICATED. handleSetKey and handleDeleteKey in internal/api/server.go check isLoopbackRequest and the rate limiter and then do the work; neither ever checks the device token, and they cannot, because auth.go:37 short-circuits the whole middleware for any loopback sender. Order #52 part (d) said 'token-protected too' and 'requires the device token EVEN ON LOOPBACK' — that is what is missing. Verified live: POST /v1/keys with no token at all reaches body validation and answers 400 about the payload, which proves nothing authenticated the caller. Consequence: any local process, and a web page the founder merely visits, can write or delete provider API keys in his Keychain and rewrite his config. The browser case is real, not theoretical: the handler reads the raw body and json.Unmarshals it without ever checking Content-Type, so a cross-site form POST using a non-preflighted content type can deliver a body that parses as valid JSON. FIX: require the device token on every MUTATING /v1 route regardless of loopback — POST /v1/keys, DELETE /v1/keys, PUT /v1/config, POST /v1/refresh — while GET routes keep the loopback exemption so the dashboard still works unauthenticated on localhost. Reject any request to the mutating routes whose Content-Type is not application/json. Return 401 for a missing or wrong token, and check the token BEFORE parsing the body, so an unauthenticated caller learns nothing about the payload shape. The embedded page must send the token it already holds on these calls.

(b) THE GROQ PROBE TOGGLE NEVER RENDERS — the same bug shape you just fixed, one field over. index.html:675 gates the toggle on p.has_probe, but HasProbe is a PARSE-TIME DISAMBIGUATOR meaning 'the YAML explicitly set probe' (defaults.go:69 sets it false, defaults.go:95 says so in a comment). With no config.yaml on this Mac it is false, so the toggle is invisible — exactly like providers:[] was. Gate the toggle on provider CAPABILITY instead: Groq is the only provider that has a probe, so the effective provider should carry something like can_probe: true for groq and the UI should render on that, with p.probe supplying the checked state. Check whether the env var USAGED_GROQ_PROBE (currently 0 in .env) feeds the displayed state, and make the page show where the value came from if env wins, the same way key_state does.

Verify: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/web -v` grows by at least 6 — POST /v1/keys with NO token is 401 on loopback; with a WRONG token is 401; with the right token succeeds against the FAKE keystore; the 401 is returned before the body is read; a non-JSON Content-Type is rejected; PUT /v1/config and POST /v1/refresh are 401 without a token on loopback; GET /v1/usage still works with no token on loopback; the settings markup renders the Groq probe toggle with NO config.yaml present. `make verify` and `make smoke` exit 0. Then rebuild and kickstart, and re-run the live check the planner ran: POST /v1/keys with no token must answer 401, not 400. Report both in your DONE line.

description: Footer collision hides the version entirely (hint is drawn over it), the hint text is stale after hold-to-flip, and the page indicator is stranded at the right leaving ~80px of dead header
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2, hostname sticks3-usage. PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 / Arduino core 2.0.17 / ESP-IDF 4.4.7, M5Unified 0.2.19 + M5GFX 0.2.28. Purity rule: gesture LOGIC goes in the pure core (firmware/src/usage/, no M5 or Arduino headers, host-tested by 'make fw-test'); only firmware/src/hal/sticks3/* and main.cpp may touch M5. Flash this over OTA ('make fw-ota'), no cable. Any upload needs Felipe's explicit authorization in the Solvr room.

Felipe on the build flashed from 490cbf9: 'top version vanished at all, show nothing. also, the pagination, way to closed to the right, leaving a huge space unused now.' Both are consequences of ORDER #51 moving seq/version out of the header, and both are arithmetic — the planner worked them out from the source, so do not treat them as taste.

(a) THE FOOTER OVERWRITES THE VERSION. screen.cpp:186-199 draws two independent strings on the same row with no fitting and no clipping: plan.footer left-aligned at x=5, then the hint 'blue: page   side: refresh' right-aligned at W - textWidth - 4. At Font0 (6 px/glyph) on a 240 px screen the hint is 26 glyphs = 156 px, so it starts at x=80. The left string 'seq 5 \xc2\xb7 v3c639cd' is 16 glyphs = 96 px and runs from x=5 to x=101. They overlap by 21 px, the hint is drawn SECOND, and the version sits at the tail of the left string — so the version is exactly what gets painted over. It gets worse as seq grows. FIX: give the footer the same measure-then-fit discipline the top bar already has in topbar.cpp — compute both widths, and when they collide shorten the HINT first (it is the least valuable text), then the seq, and never the version. The version is the thing Felipe asked to keep visible.

(b) THE HINT TEXT IS ALSO STALE. It still reads 'side: refresh', but as of 490cbf9 the side button does two things: click refreshes and a 1.5 s hold flips the screen. Nothing on the display says the flip exists, so it is undiscoverable. Rewrite the hint to cover both without bloating it — something like 'blue: page  side: refresh / hold: flip', and note that whatever you choose feeds directly into (a), since a longer hint collides sooner. Shorter is better here.

(c) THE PAGE INDICATOR IS STRANDED ON THE RIGHT. topbar.cpp:78-88 packs strictly right-to-left — wifi dot, then battery gauge and label, then the page indicator immediately left of them — while the title stays pinned at x=5. With version and asOf gone from the header, the indicator lands near x=133 while the title ends around x=53, leaving roughly 80 px of dead space in the middle of the bar. That is what Felipe means by 'huge space unused'. FIX: once the always-drawn right-hand cluster is placed, CENTRE the page indicator in the free span between the title's right edge and the cluster's left edge, instead of butting it against the cluster. Keep the existing drop-precedence — the indicator still disappears before the title when space runs out — and keep it from ever overlapping either neighbour.

Verify: extend test_topbar.cpp and add footer-layout tests, at least 6 new — the page indicator is centred in the free span for a 240 px bar with a short title; it still drops before the title when the bar is narrow; it never overlaps the battery label; the footer version survives when seq is 3 digits; the hint is shortened rather than the version when they collide; and the footer never draws past the screen edge. `make fw-test` Failed 0 and `make fw-build` SUCCESS. Then the flash is Felipe's call, over OTA via firmware/scripts/upload_ota.sh — you do not run it, and the task does not flip until he confirms he can read the version and that the top bar looks balanced.

DEFECT found reviewing 5922b21 — the fitting logic and the centring are BOTH CORRECT and the tests are honest, but the hint text became unreadable: screen.cpp:192 now reads 'blue: page   side: r/h'. 'r/h' communicates nothing to a human, and the whole reason this line exists is discoverability — an abbreviation nobody can decode is worse than the stale text it replaced. The arithmetic also shows it does not even fit: at Font0 the left string 'seq 5 \xc2\xb7 v3c639cd' is 96 px, avail is 240-5-4 = 231, so the hint budget is 231-96-4 = 131 px = 21 glyphs, while 'blue: page   side: r/h' is 22 glyphs = 132 px — so fitRight is truncating it on top of the abbreviation. FIX, in this order: (1) DROP 'seq N' from the footer entirely. Felipe asked for the VERSION, never the seq; seq is developer noise and it is already on the serial line and in the snapshot. That frees 8 glyphs and lifts the hint budget to 231-48-4 = 179 px = 29 glyphs. (2) Write the hint in WHOLE WORDS within that budget — no single-letter codes, no 'r/h', nothing a reader has to decode. Two of the three actions in plain words beats three in cipher; the hold gesture also announces itself with the amber hint once a hold starts, so it is not solely dependent on this line. (3) Keep the fitting rules exactly as built — hint shortens first, version never shortens — and keep footerCompute's seq-dropping branch for the case where a future left string grows. Add a test asserting the rendered hint contains no single-character token between separators, so this cannot regress into cipher again.

description: Prove deep sleep from the request cadence: the agent logs no incoming requests at all, so add an access log and expose per-client last-seen/interval/304-split (firmware RTC counters only if that leaves ambiguity)
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2, hostname sticks3-usage. PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 / Arduino core 2.0.17 / ESP-IDF 4.4.7, M5Unified 0.2.19 + M5GFX 0.2.28. Purity rule: gesture LOGIC goes in the pure core (firmware/src/usage/, no M5 or Arduino headers, host-tested by 'make fw-test'); only firmware/src/hal/sticks3/* and main.cpp may touch M5. Flash this over OTA ('make fw-ota'), no cable. Any upload needs Felipe's explicit authorization in the Solvr room.

Felipe: 'does deep sleep REALLY occurs, can you validate?' — then, when told the firmware answer was invisible without a cable: 'you can infer via how many times client checked the api =)'. He is right, and it makes most of the original plan unnecessary. The device's FETCH CADENCE already encodes its power state, and it costs no firmware change at all. Do this in two parts, host first, and STOP after part one if it answers the question.

PART ONE, HOST ONLY, NO FIRMWARE — the agent currently logs NO incoming requests whatsoever. Verified: usaged.out.log holds only poller warnings, and internal/api has no access log. Add one: for every request to /v1/usage, log the timestamp, the client address, the method, whether it answered 200 or 304, and the If-None-Match it presented. Keep the latest per client in memory and expose it as device state on /v1/usage and the Attention tab — last seen, seconds since, observed interval, and the 200/304 split. The cadence is the evidence: on USB the device polls every 300 s like clockwork, and on battery it sleeps instead, so a gap far longer than 300 s followed by a resumption IS deep sleep, and the 60 s timer backstop should show as a roughly minute-by-minute rhythm rather than the 300 s one. Do not log the device token or any header that carries it.

PART TWO, ONLY IF PART ONE LEAVES REAL AMBIGUITY — the cadence proves THAT it slept, not WHY it woke. If and only if that distinction matters after Felipe has looked at part one, keep a wake counter, last wake cause and sleep count in RTC_DATA_ATTR (they survive deep sleep) and report them on the next fetch via query parameters or a small header. Do not build this speculatively. fmtWake and fmtSleep already exist at serial_proto.cpp:104 and :111 and main.cpp:433 already reads the cause and discards it, so the firmware work is small — but it is still firmware, and firmware needs a flash and a UAT that part one does not.

THE INVARIANT, if part two happens: the report rides on the REQUEST, so it must not perturb the ETag / If-None-Match path, must not change rev, and must not cause a redraw. A 304 stays a 304 and the screen must not repaint. Assert it in a test rather than assuming it.

Verify part one: `go test ./internal/api -v` grows by at least 4 — a request is logged with its status; the 200/304 split is counted correctly; the observed interval is computed from real timestamps; and NO token value ever appears in a log line. `make verify` and `make smoke` exit 0, then rebuild and kickstart. The UAT needs no cable and no flash: Felipe unplugs the device, waits a few minutes, and reads the last-seen and interval figures in his browser — a stalled last-seen while the screen is dark, and a resumption on button press, is the proof he asked for.

description: Crit banner text sits 2 px high in its red rect (cursor y=118 in a rect centred on y=124) and is centred on the screen rather than on the rect
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2, hostname sticks3-usage. PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 / Arduino core 2.0.17 / ESP-IDF 4.4.7, M5Unified 0.2.19 + M5GFX 0.2.28.
