description: [WITHDRAWN 2026-09-07 — not built] PROVISIONING 4/4: change Wi-Fi from the Settings page — the everyday case, once the device is already reachable
steps: Context: usaged (Go, stdlib only, zero external dependencies) at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. House rules in AGENTS.md; invariants in GOLDEN_RULES.md. internal/web/ is embedded with go:embed — nothing there is live until 'make build && launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.usaged'.

WHY THIS EXISTS (read once, applies to all four provisioning tasks): secrets.h is a COMPILE-TIME header, so WIFI_SSID, WIFI_PASS, USAGED_HOST, USAGED_DEVICE_TOKEN and OTA_PASS become plaintext strings inside firmware.bin — verified with `strings` against a real build. Publishing that binary to M5Burner would hand out the builder's Wi-Fi password, and a stranger's flash could not work anyway because it would try to join OUR SSID and reach OUR Mac. The goal of this group is a binary that carries NO credentials and a device a stranger can set up without a cable, a build step, or a file. THE DECISIVE CONSTRAINT: every off-the-shelf provisioning framework (Espressif WiFiProv, Improv, WiFiManager) conveys Wi-Fi CREDENTIALS ONLY. This device additionally needs to learn WHICH AGENT to talk to and to obtain a DEVICE TOKEN, so a custom portal that collects all four in one screen beats a generic app that solves half and leaves a second setup step. Build order matters and is not negotiable: credentials store first, then the portal that fills it, then pairing, then the everyday editing path. A pairing code cannot help a device that is not yet on the network.

Felipe's original request: 'We need to set the Wi-Fi from the web UI. Under settings.' This is the LAST of the four, not the first, and the ordering is the design rather than a preference: the Settings page is served by the Mac, so a device that has never joined a network cannot reach it to be told how. The portal bootstraps; Settings maintains. Building this first would produce a feature that works for every device except a new one.

THE CHANNEL DOES NOT EXIST YET — build it first, and do not assume the snapshot can carry this. Verified against the current code: the device polls GET /v1/usage and parses only v, rev, seq, generated_at, next_sec, age and providers (model.cpp:69-91). There is NO server-to-device configuration path. GET /v1/device is server-to-BROWSER (device state for the dashboard) and is not read by the firmware at all. Putting Wi-Fi settings into the snapshot is the WRONG fix: the snapshot body is hashed into rev, so device-bound config would churn rev and force redraws — breaking the redraw-only-on-change invariant this whole project rests on, exactly as an unhashed age field had to be kept outside it. Add a SEPARATE endpoint the device polls for pending device-directed settings, carrying no ETag and never touching rev, in the same spirit as GET /v1/device. Keep it small: a pending-change record the device acknowledges, so a change is applied once rather than on every poll. Note the latency this implies — a change lands on the device's next poll, not instantly — and say so in the UI rather than letting it look broken.

Add a Wi-Fi section to the Settings tab showing the network the device is currently on, with fields to change it. The device applies new credentials and re-joins. THE FAILURE PATH IS THE IMPORTANT PART: if the new credentials do not work the device has just been told to leave a working network for a broken one, so it must fall back — first to the previous credentials if they still work, and otherwise to the portal from task 2. Never leave the user with a dark device and a cable as the only recovery. Say plainly in the UI that a change may take the device offline briefly.

Respect the boundaries already established: the Wi-Fi password is a credential, so it is never returned by GET /v1/config, never rendered back into the page, and never logged — the same treatment key_state gets today, showing only whether it is set. Follow the key_source labelling convention so the UI says where the value actually lives rather than implying the dashboard owns it.

Verify: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/web -v` gains tests that the password is write-only through the API, that GET never discloses it, and that an invalid payload changes nothing. `make verify` and `make smoke` exit 0; rebuild and kickstart, then confirm in a REAL BROWSER rather than by curl — the point is the page. UAT with Felipe: he moves the device to a different network from the dashboard, and separately confirms that entering a deliberately wrong password brings the device back rather than stranding it.

AMENDED BY SPIKE (2026-09-06) — unchanged in mechanism: there is still NO server-to-device configuration channel, and it must be a SEPARATE endpoint that carries no ETag and never touches rev, or the redraw-only-on-change invariant breaks. One measured addition to the failure path: because AP_STA is single-channel, a device that leaves a working network for a bad one and falls back to the portal will DROP any phone already associated to that portal when it retries the join. The recovery UX must therefore live on the DEVICE SCREEN, not in the browser session.

description: [DEFERRED by decision 2026-09-07] OPTIONAL v3: task-hub rows — accept external rows via POST /v1/rows so agent/task status can share the same snapshot and screen
steps: Snapshot v1 (the ONE contract every client uses; keep it under 1 KB): `{"v":1,"seq":<int, +1 only when rev changes>,"rev":"<8 hex>","generated_at":<unix s of the last CHANGE>,"checked_at":<unix s of the last poll attempt>,"next_sec":900,"providers":[{"id":"claude","label":"Claude","plan":"max_20x","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"CLAUDE 5h","pct":19,"txt":"05:09","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788411000},{"k":"7d","label":"CLAUDE 7d","pct":30,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000},{"k":"7d:Fable","label":"FABLE 7d","pct":20,"txt":"Mon","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788768000}]},{"id":"codex","label":"ChatGPT","plan":"plus","status":"ok","msg":"","rows":[{"k":"5h","label":"GPT 5h","pct":100,"txt":"23:13","tier":"crit","reset_at":1788401621},{"k":"7d","label":"GPT 7d","pct":31,"txt":"Tue","tier":"ok","reset_at":1788969665},{"k":"bal","label":"GPT bal","pct":null,"txt":"$178.10","tier":"ok","reset_at":null}]}]}`. Provider ids in fixed order: claude, codex, openrouter:main, openrouter:fallback, groq. status ∈ ok|stale|auth|error|off; msg is a ≤24-char human hint ("run claude", "run codex", "429 until 21:40", "no key"). rows[].label ≤10 chars, txt ≤11 chars, pct int or null, tier ∈ ok|warn|crit|off (ok <50, warn 50-79, crit ≥80; off when pct null or status not ok/stale). `rev` = first 8 hex chars of sha256 over the canonical JSON array `[[id,status,plan,[[k,pct,txt,tier],…]],…]` (rows in order, no whitespace, pct null encoded as null) — NOTE: checked_at, generated_at, reset_at, msg and label are NOT part of the hash, so a countdown never changes rev, but any status/tier/pct/txt change does.

Add `POST /v1/rows` (token required): body `{"id":"tasks","label":"Tasks","ttl_sec":1200,"rows":[{"k":"run","label":"bart2 run","pct":null,"txt":"12m","tier":"ok"}]}` → stored as an extra provider block (id must start with `ext:`; validated like any provider; expires after ttl_sec → removed → rev changes). This is the lean equivalent of TaskHub's `/ingest`, kept inside the one snapshot contract so the web page and the firmware page 2 show it with zero new client code. Document in README.
Verify: `go test ./internal/api -run Rows -v | grep -c '^--- PASS'` ≥ 3 (accept, reject bad id, expiry changes rev); `make smoke` exits 0; `make verify` exits 0.

description: ORDER #51: rebalance header and footer — move seq/version out of the top bar into the footer, widen wifi-battery gap
steps: Firmware context: M5StickS3 unit #2, hostname sticks3-usage. PlatformIO espressif32@6.12.0 / Arduino core 2.0.17 / ESP-IDF 4.4.7, M5Unified 0.2.19 + M5GFX 0.2.28. Fresh-clone build must stay green. Any upload needs Felipe's explicit authorization in the Solvr room.

(1) The HEADER keeps only page title, page indicator, battery gauge and link dot — remove the version string and 'seq N' from the top bar entirely. They are no longer drawn there; screen.cpp's drawPlan no longer calls topbar version or asOf positions.

(2) MOVE 'seq' and the version to the FOOTER beside the button hint. The footer reads: 'seq N · v<7char-sha> · blue: page  side: refresh' (left-aligned 'seq · version', right-aligned button hint). The footer spans full width and previously carried only the button hint, so there is room.

description: PROD-READY 1/10: the Settings page's provider controls are frozen at daemon startup — the 'enabled' checkbox AND a newly saved API key both do nothing until a restart, because buildFetchers runs once [AUDIT #20 + the 2026-09-07 OpenRouter key report]
steps: Context (repeat in your head before every task; the loop starts you with no memory): this repo is ai-usage (Go module name `usaged`) at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage — Felipe's AI-usage monitor. A Go daemon on this Mac polls Claude / ChatGPT-Codex / OpenRouter / Groq quotas every 900 s and serves a dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8765; M5StickS3 firmware renders the same snapshot. Go 1.26.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/go, stdlib only, ZERO external Go dependencies (~/go/bin/staticcheck for lint). House rules in AGENTS.md, invariants in GOLDEN_RULES.md. spec.json at the repo root is BOTH the acceptance ledger and the executable build order (92 tasks): take the first entry with `passes: false`, do its steps exactly, run its literal `Verify:` step, and only then flip that one boolean to true (re-read the file from disk, change one boolean, keep the task count unchanged). Tasks 85-92 are the prod-readiness group and every one of them comes from docs/handovers/2026-09-07-prod-readiness/ — HANDOVER.md (why), AUDIT.md (20 confirmed findings with reproduction commands), PLAN-r1.md (approved 2026-09-07). Read AUDIT.md finding #20 before starting this one.

THE LANE — non-negotiable, and the reason every bug on 2026-09-07 was found. internal/web/ is embedded with go:embed, so NOTHING you change there is live until you rebuild AND restart. A green `go test` proves nothing across a process boundary: nine bugs shipped on 2026-09-07 and every one had a passing test faking the exact thing that was broken (FakeKeyStore, httptest, a grep over index.html that never parsed the JS). After every Go change run, in this order: (1) `make verify` — fmt vet lint test build, 13/13 today; (2) `cp bin/ai-usage ~/.local/bin/ai-usage`; (3) `codesign --force --sign - ~/.local/bin/ai-usage` — `make build` output is UNSIGNED and an unsigned copy gets the daemon killed with OS_REASON_CODESIGNING; (4) `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.ai-usage`; (5) `lsof -nP -iTCP:8765 -sTCP:LISTEN` and confirm the PID is launchd's. NEVER hand-start the daemon on 8765: it prevents launchd from binding, nothing persists across a reboot, and every conclusion drawn from the log afterwards is worthless. The launchd label is `com.fcavalcanti.ai-usage` — the old `com.fcavalcanti.usaged` spelling in older spec.json steps is stale.

THE DEFECT, verified live on 2026-09-07 against the running daemon: unchecking a provider in Settings and saving returns ok:true, writes `enabled: false` to the YAML, and reads back as disabled on the next visit — while the scheduler keeps polling that provider forever. `grep -rn --include='*.go' 'EffectiveProviders|ProviderConfigs' internal cmd | grep -v _test.go` has NO hit inside cmd/usaged/once.go, and the only `Enabled` token in buildFetchers (once.go:91-183) is the unrelated `cfg.GroqProbeEnabled()` at once.go:176. Not 'until restart' — forever, because a restart re-runs the same buildFetchers that has never heard of the flag. spec.json TASK 47 (array index 46, 'Single YAML config file for keys, per-provider toggles, labels and alerts') is marked passes:true while its own Verify step reads, verbatim: "`enabled: false` drops the provider from the snapshot and changes the rev." The config tests only assert YAML parse/serialize round-trips, which is why the suite is green over a rule the code has never honoured. Do NOT flip task 47 in this task — completing this one simply makes 47 honestly true.

THE SAME DEFECT, SECOND SYMPTOM — reported live by Felipe 2026-09-07 ~19:45 and reproduced on the running daemon before it was written down: he saved the OpenRouter main and fallback keys in the dashboard, the UI confirmed them, he reset the StickS3, and nothing changed. Evidence: both keys ARE in the keychain (`security find-generic-password -s usaged -a openrouter:main` succeeds, 73-char value) while `GET /v1/usage` still returns openrouter:main and openrouter:fallback as `status: off, msg: 'no key'` — which is `newStaticFetcher(b.id, b.label, "no key")` from once.go:165. The daemon had been up 2h21m (started 17:24:03), i.e. BEFORE the keys were saved. Root cause is identical to the enabled flag: buildFetchers reads the keychain exactly once at cmd/usaged/serve.go:58 (once.go:150-153 for OpenRouter, once.go:171-174 for Groq) and the fetcher list is then frozen for the life of the process. internal/api/server.go handleSetKey (:788-833) and handleDeleteKey (:836-862) write the keychain and answer ok:true WITHOUT touching s.sched — verified by reading both handlers end to end. The device is innocent: it renders whatever the daemon serves, so resetting the stick can never fix it.

WHY THE FIX GOES IN buildFetchers AND NOT IN A FILTER AT THE API LAYER (checked in the code; do not 'simplify' this away): internal/sched/scheduler.go:173-178 rebuilds the provider block list strictly from `s.Fetchers` and then calls `snapshot.Apply`, which recomputes rev and bumps seq. So dropping a fetcher genuinely removes the provider from the snapshot AND changes the rev, which is exactly what spec task 47's Verify step demands. Filtering inside handleUsage instead would serve a body that no longer matches its own `rev`, and the device's ETag/rev change detection would silently break.

(a) In cmd/usaged/once.go, make `buildFetchers(cfg config.Config, ks creds.KeyStore)` walk `cfg.EffectiveProviders()` (internal/config/defaults.go:164) and SKIP any provider whose `Enabled` is false. Claude (once.go:114-133) and Codex (once.go:135-147) are unconditional today and must become conditional like OpenRouter and Groq. Provider ids come from config.DefaultProviderOrder — claude, codex, openrouter:main, openrouter:fallback, groq — and are the same ids the fetchers report from `f.ID()`. Do NOT reorder anything: canonical order is already enforced downstream by `snapshot.Order` (scheduler.go:184).

(b) Add `func (s *Scheduler) SetFetchers(f []providers.Fetcher)` to internal/sched/scheduler.go, guarded by `s.pollMu` — the SAME mutex PollOnce (scheduler.go:78) and Refresh (scheduler.go:330) already hold across the whole poll, which is where `s.Fetchers` is read at :101 and :173. Model it on the existing `SetInterval` (scheduler.go:352) so there is ONE established shape for a runtime setting change, not two. Document in the doc comment that the new list takes effect on the next poll.

(c) internal/api cannot call buildFetchers — it lives in `package main`. It returns exactly: {"usage":{"rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":5,"resetsAt":"2026-09-08T04:23:36.686Z"},"weekly":{"status":"ok","percent":2,"resetsAt":"2026-09-14T00:00:00.686Z"},"monthly":{"status":"ok","percent":1,"resetsAt":"2026-10-07T23:14:35.686Z"}}}. TRAPS THE SPIKE ALREADY WALKED INTO, so you do not repeat them: (1) The OpenCode ZEN base `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` has NO usage route — /zen/v1/usage is 404. Only the GO base `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` has one. Using the Go key against the Zen base gives a confusing 500. (2) `api.opencode.ai` is a DIFFERENT host that answers 200 'Hello, world!' at / and 200 'Not Found' for every usage path — it is not the source, and its 200-on-missing-route will fool a naive status check. (3) The console at opencode.ai/workspace/<id>/go is a SolidStart app using SERVER FUNCTIONS, not REST; its JS bundles contain no API paths. Do NOT scrape it. (4) The API is COARSER than the webui: three integer percentages and reset times, with NO per-model rows and NO dollar figures. The webui's 'GPT 5.6 Luna $0.06 / $3.00' table comes from those server functions. Render percentages only — never invent a dollar amount. (a) NEW PROVIDER `internal/providers/opencode.go`, modelled on openrouter.go: a providers.Fetcher with ID() and Fetch(ctx, now) using the shared httpx.Client. (b) ROW MAPPING, three rows: rolling -> K "5h", weekly -> K "7d", monthly -> K "30d". `percent` (an integer) -> Row.Pct; `resetsAt` is RFC3339 WITH MILLISECONDS -> Row.ResetAt as unix seconds (parse with time.RFC3339, which accepts the fractional part; a parse failure must leave ResetAt nil, never zero). Row.Tier via format.Tier, provider Severity via format.Severity. A window whose upstream `status` is not "ok" gets tier `off` and a nil Pct rather than a fabricated number.

(c) `30d` IS A NEW WINDOW KEY — Row.K has only ever carried "5h" and "7d". Task 86 introduced format.Alerts.WarnPctFor(k); extend it so "30d" maps to the WEEKLY threshold (quota_warn_weekly_pct, default 60), NOT the 5h one. Felipe's reasoning, recorded so nobody flips it back: a monthly cap you cannot recover from deserves the earlier warning. Add a test that a 30d row at 62% warns while a 5h row at 62% does not.

(d) `internal/config/defaults.go` — add `ProviderOpenCodeGo = "opencode:go"`, append it to DefaultProviderOrder and to DefaultProviders() with label `OpenCode Go` and KeyEnv `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. `internal/config/config.go` — read OPENCODE_API_KEY with the same env-then-keychain precedence the OpenRouter and Groq keys already use.

(f) `cmd/usaged/once.go` buildFetchers — construct it exactly like the Groq block: env key first, keychain fallback, `newStaticFetcher(id, label, "no key")` when neither source has one. It must honour the Enabled flag and the live key rebuild that task 85 added — call the same code, do not write a second mechanism.

(g) DASHBOARD — check `internal/web/index.html` renders the provider grid, the Settings provider rows and the Needs-attention list from the config/snapshot GENERICALLY. If any of them is hardcoded to five providers or to the five known ids, that is a second spelling: drive it off the payload instead. The `30d` row needs a display label; reuse whatever pattern the existing 5h/7d rows use rather than inventing a new one.

THEN widen the array to [6]. The clamp is the bug; the widening is the feature.

A Go daemon serves a snapshot on 127.0.0.1:8765; the dashboard and the M5StickS3 both render it. Go, stdlib only, ZERO external dependencies. spec.json is both the acceptance ledger and the build order. DEPENDS ON task 92 (OpenCode Go) — that task adds a 6th provider and widens the firmware provider array, and this task reorders whatever set exists.

THE LANE — non-negotiable: `make verify`, `cp bin/ai-usage ~/.local/bin/ai-usage`, `codesign --force --sign - ~/.local/bin/ai-usage` (unsigned copies get the daemon killed with OS_REASON_CODESIGNING), `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.ai-usage`, `lsof -nP -iTCP:8765 -sTCP:LISTEN` with launchd's PID. NEVER hand-start on 8765. internal/web/ is go:embed — the page is not live until you rebuild AND restart.

WHY FELIPE WANTS THIS (his words, 2026-09-07): 'on sticks3, that goes a long way — pick exactly first top two, it's what's on first page'. The device shows 5 rows per page (render_plan.cpp:165 maxLines = 5). Claude and Codex contribute 3 rows each, so page 1 today is Claude's three rows plus Codex's first two. Choosing the order therefore chooses what he sees without pressing a button. This is a usability feature, not decoration.

THE GOOD NEWS, VERIFIED IN THE FIRMWARE: the device already renders in PAYLOAD ORDER. render_plan.cpp:156 and :357 walk m.providers[i] in the order the JSON delivered them, filtered by kind, and model.cpp parses them in array order. Nothing re-sorts by id. So once the daemon emits a different order, the StickS3 obeys it with NO firmware change. Do not add a sort to the firmware.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT, AND FELIPE MUST BE TOLD IT IN THE DONE LINE: the device groups pages by KIND before order — kKindOrder at render_plan.cpp:149 is a fixed plan -> credit -> free sequence. So reordering can only move a provider WITHIN its kind. A credit provider (the OpenRouter blocks) can never be dragged onto page 1 ahead of the plan providers unless kKindOrder itself changes, and that is a separate decision that is Felipe's to make. State this limit plainly rather than shipping a Settings control that silently ignores half the drags.

THE BLOCKER TO SOLVE: internal/snapshot/types.go:11-13 declares canonicalProviderOrder as 'the fixed order every client expects', and Validate at types.go:90-91 REJECTS any snapshot whose providers are not in that exact order with `provider %s out of canonical order`. A user-chosen order is by definition not that fixed order, so Validate must change or every reordered snapshot is refused.

(a) CONFIG — add an ordered list of provider ids to the YAML config and to the PUT /v1/config body, persisted like the existing provider entries. Do NOT invent a second representation: the config already carries a provider list (config.ProviderConfigs / EffectiveProviders at defaults.go:164) and DefaultProviderOrder is the default. The order the user chooses replaces DefaultProviderOrder as the source of truth for display order; unknown or missing ids fall back to their default position so a stale config can never drop a provider.

(b) SNAPSHOT — snapshot.Order(ids) (types.go:126) must sort by the CONFIGURED order rather than the package-level constant, and Validate must stop asserting a global canonical sequence. Keep the checks that still mean something: no duplicate ids, no unknown ids, every id known to the config. Update the doc comment at types.go:9-10, which currently states the order is fixed — leaving that comment is exactly the kind of stale prose that misleads the next reader.

(c) REV MUST CHANGE WHEN THE ORDER CHANGES. snapshot.Rev hashes the provider blocks; confirm with a test that two snapshots with identical providers in different orders produce DIFFERENT revs and therefore bump Seq. description: [BLOCKED — no balance API exists] OpenCode Zen as a credit provider: show the account balance in dollars, exactly like OpenRouter. Spiked exhaustively 2026-09-07; ship it the day OpenCode exposes a key-authenticated balance route
steps: Context: this repo is ai-usage at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. Felipe holds BOTH OpenCode subscriptions: Go (a quota subscription, shipped as task 92, kind `plan`) and Zen (pay-as-you-go CREDIT, browser shows 'Current balance $6.87'). He wants Zen rendered like OpenRouter and Groq: kind `credit`, one row, a dollar balance, nothing else. That design is settled and correct — the ONLY thing missing is a source.

WHY THIS IS BLOCKED, WITH THE DECISIVE TEST — do NOT re-spike it. On 2026-09-07 roughly 45 candidate paths were probed with a valid key across three hosts (opencode.ai, api.opencode.ai, app.opencode.ai), both API bases (/zen/v1 and /zen/go/v1), and BOTH auth styles (`Authorization: Bearer` and `x-api-key`): usage, credits, balance, billing, wallet, key, me, account, limits, subscription, quota, organization/costs, the OpenAI-legacy dashboard/billing/credit_grants and dashboard/billing/subscription, plus workspace-scoped and query-parameter variants. Every response was additionally grepped for the known balance 6.87/687 as an oracle. ZERO matches. THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT MAKES THIS CONCLUSIVE: on this host a route that EXISTS but gets the wrong auth header returns 401 JSON {"type":"error","error":{"type":"AuthError",...}}, while a route that DOES NOT EXIST falls through to the marketing SPA and returns 404 HTML. `/zen/go/v1/usage` with x-api-key returns 401 (real route, wrong header). EVERY balance candidate returns 404-SPA under BOTH auth styles. They are not mis-authenticated — they are absent.

THE DOCS AGREE. https://opencode.ai/docs/zen was read in full: its 'Endpoints' section lists ONLY per-model inference endpoints (GPT -> https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses, Anthropic -> https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages). The balance appears exactly once, as prose in the Auto-reload section: 'If your balance goes below $5, Zen will automatically reload $20.' There is no documented balance API and no undocumented one that answers.

THE NEAREST THING THAT DOES EXIST, and why it is not enough: a successful `POST /zen/v1/responses` returns a top-level `cost` field (measured 0.00002015 USD for a 22-token call) alongside the usual `usage` block. That is PER-REQUEST SPEND, not an account balance. It cannot be summed into $6.87 without a starting balance the API never exposes, and this daemon does not proxy Felipe's inference traffic anyway. Do not try to derive a balance from it — a computed number that drifts from the real one is worse than no number.

WHERE THE NUMBER ACTUALLY LIVES: the console at opencode.ai/workspace/<id> is a SolidStart app and the balance is produced by a SERVER FUNCTION — the client bundle index-CMfgHWZM.js contains createServerReference("57febdb66fa462161adef94258b3557858a7bcae013f15c2b7de85d2094182d9") and five siblings. POST https://opencode.ai/_server with that id is LIVE but answers {"status":500,"unhandled":true,"message":"HTTPError"} for an API-key caller: it is authenticated by the browser SESSION COOKIE, not by the API key.

DO NOT BUILD A COOKIE SCRAPER. It would depend on an undocumented internal RPC, a serialized argument format that changes with every deploy, and an expiring browser session Felipe would have to re-paste — and it would fail silently into a wrong number on the dashboard and the StickS3. docs/SOURCES.md's Policy section is explicit that this project reads documented, stable, key-authenticated sources only. A provider that cannot state a real number must not render one.

TRIGGER TO UNBLOCK: re-run exactly one probe — `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/usage` and the same against /zen/v1/credits and /zen/v1/balance. If any returns JSON containing a balance, this task becomes buildable in an afternoon and everything below applies. Until one of them does, leave this task [BLOCKED] and skip it.

(a) WHEN UNBLOCKED — provider id `opencode:zen`, label `OpenCode Zen`, kind `credit` so the firmware groups it with the OpenRouter blocks on the CREDITS page rather than the plan pages. Sits directly after `opencode:go` in config.DefaultProviderOrder and in snapshot.canonicalProviderOrder.

(b) ONE ROW, the balance, formatted with format.Money(format.Cents(usd)) exactly as openrouter.go:170 does — never a bare float, never a percentage. Row K `bal`, label `ZEN bal`. Reuse the OpenRouter low-balance severity override at openrouter.go:176-187 so the alerts threshold quota/openrouter_low_usd (task 86 made it configurable) drives Zen too, or add a sibling knob if Felipe wants them independent — ASK, do not assume.

(c) NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS IT: the Zen and Go API keys are BYTE-IDENTICAL — one credential serves both products (verified by comparing ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json entries `opencode` and `opencode-go`). So OPENCODE_API_KEY covers both providers and no second key or second .env variable is needed. Do not add one.

(d) The firmware provider array was already widened to [6] and clamped by task 92. A SEVENTH provider needs model.h:44 bumped again to [7] AND the clamp re-checked — the clamp makes an over-long payload safe, but the seventh block would be silently dropped rather than shown. Widen it in the same commit.

Verify (only once unblocked): `make verify` green with a fixture for the real balance payload. Then THE LANE (make verify, cp, `codesign --force --sign - ~/.local/bin/ai-usage`, launchctl kickstart, lsof) and prove on the RUNNING daemon that `curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/v1/usage` shows opencode:zen with one row whose dollar amount MATCHES the balance shown at opencode.ai in the browser at the same moment — paste both. The key must never appear in any output.

THIS TASK IS [BLOCKED] AND THE LOOP MUST SKIP IT. It is not yours to run: no amount of code makes a number that no endpoint returns. Felipe unblocks it by confirming OpenCode has shipped a balance route.

description: "Use this next": a 4-hour provider recommendation, computed once in the daemon, shown on the dashboard and behind the reserved BtnA HOLD gesture
steps: Context (repeat in your head; the loop starts you with no memory): this repo is ai-usage at /Users/fcavalcanti/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage. A Go daemon polls quota providers and serves a dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8765; M5StickS3 firmware renders the same snapshot. Go, stdlib only, ZERO external dependencies. spec.json is both the acceptance ledger and the executable build order (96 tasks). Tasks 85-93 are done; 95 is Felipe's closing sweep and is NOT yours. This task is NEW work agreed with Felipe on 2026-09-08.

THE LANE — non-negotiable: `make verify`, `cp bin/ai-usage /Users/fcavalcanti/.local/bin/ai-usage`, `codesign --force --sign - /Users/fcavalcanti/.local/bin/ai-usage` (unsigned copies get the daemon killed with OS_REASON_CODESIGNING), `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.fcavalcanti.ai-usage`, `lsof -nP -iTCP:8765 -sTCP:LISTEN` with launchd's PID. NEVER hand-start on 8765. internal/web/ is go:embed — the page is not live until you rebuild AND restart.

WHAT FELIPE WANTS: one answer to 'which provider should I use for the next 4 hours', instead of him deriving it from five providers and a dozen percentages every session. Horizon is FIXED at 4 hours — do not add a config knob for it. Only subscription plans compete; prepaid credit is mentioned only as a fallback when every plan is exhausted, because plan quota is sunk cost while credit is real marginal spend.

THE CALCULATION — three things bind at once, and a naive 'lowest percentage wins' gets it wrong. (1) A WINDOW THAT RESETS INSIDE THE HORIZON IS WORTH ITS FULL BUDGET, not its current remainder: measured live 2026-09-08, claude's 5h sat at 25% but reset in 0.2h, so for 3.8 of the next 4 hours a fresh window was available; scoring it on the 25% would rank it far too low. (2) THE LONG WINDOW IS USUALLY THE REAL CAP — effective capacity is min(short-window headroom, long-window headroom); claude's weekly at 58% with 126h to go was the actual limit, not its 5h. (3) PACE RATIO = quota_used_fraction / time_elapsed_fraction; >1 means burning faster than the window refills. Measured that day: codex 5h=0% 7d=0% pace 0.0x; claude 5h=25% (resets 0.2h) 7d=58% (resets 126h) pace 2.3x; opencode:go 5h=18% (resets 3.9h) 7d=73% (resets 118h) pace 2.4x. Correct answer that moment: CODEX, decisively; claude second; opencode:go last (73% of the week gone with 5 days left).

(a) `internal/advise/advise.go` — NEW, PURE, NO I/O. Signature takes []snapshot.Provider plus a now time.Time and a horizon time.Duration, returns a ranked []Recommendation{ID, Label, Score, PaceRatio, EffectiveHeadroomPct, Reason}. Pure so it is host-testable with fixed clocks. Derive each row's window length from Row.K ("5h", "7d", "30d" — the 30d key was added by task 92); NEVER hardcode a window length per provider id. Row.ResetAt gives the reset instant.

(b) Only providers whose kind is "plan" are ranked. Credit providers (kind "credit") are NOT ranked and do not compete — surface them as a single fallback note only when every plan is exhausted or over pace. Do not invent a price-per-token to convert a dollar balance into a percentage; that number would be fabricated and this project does not ship fabricated figures.

(c) `internal/api` — add `GET /v1/advise` returning the ranking as JSON. IT MUST STAY OUT OF /v1/usage: the advice changes whenever any percentage moves, and snapshot.Rev is hashed over the provider blocks, so folding it into the snapshot would churn rev on nearly every poll and make the device redraw constantly. Follow the existing auth shape — loopback-exempt GET, token required from the LAN.

(d) DASHBOARD — a card at the top of internal/web/index.html showing the winner, the one-line reason, and the pace ratio per provider so the reasoning is inspectable rather than magic. It renders from /v1/advise. Do NOT re-derive any threshold or ranking in JavaScript: the daemon is the single source of truth, and two of 2026-09-07's nine bugs were exactly a second spelling of a constant.

(e) FIRMWARE, pure core: `firmware/src/usage/advise_view.{h,cpp}` formats the response into the 240x135 layout. No M5 or Arduino headers — it lives in the pure core and is host-tested by `make fw-test`.

(f) FIX THE HOLD THRESHOLD, or the gesture cannot fire at all. docs/DEVICES.md:111 already diagnoses it: BtnA HOLD does nothing because the 600 ms threshold set in board.cpp lets the click detector consume the event before M5.BtnA.wasHold() sees it. Raise it to 1500 ms, matching BtnB. Felipe has reported blue-hold 'does nothing' more than once; this is the fix AND the reason the gesture was reserved.

(g) `firmware/src/main.cpp` — BtnA HOLD fetches /v1/advise and renders the overlay; any button dismisses it. It is a TRANSIENT OVERLAY, not a new page in the cycle: single-click paging must behave exactly as before. ORDER #72 / task 72 reserved this gesture for 'a future AI-agent action' — this is that action, so update the reservation note rather than leaving it claiming the hold is unbound.

(h) DO NOT PUT THIS IN THE FOOTER, and do not use the spare line. `char footer[25]` (render_plan.h:47) already carries the version plus the button hint and sheds content on collision via footerCompute — there is no room. And pages 2-4 only have a spare 5th line because six providers happen to produce 9/4/4 rows; a seventh provider takes that spare away silently, which is precisely the kind of hidden assumption tasks 85-93 spent a day removing.
(i) `docs/DEVICES.md` — move BtnA HOLD in the button map from **reserved** to the new action, and record the 600 ms -> 1500 ms threshold change with the reason. Leave the BtnB rows alone.

Verify: `make verify` exits 0 with internal/advise tests covering a reset landing INSIDE the horizon, one landing just OUTSIDE it, a provider capped by its long window rather than its short one, and all-plans-exhausted falling back to the credit note. `make fw-test` Failed 0 with advise_view layout tests. Then run THE LANE and prove it on the RUNNING daemon: `curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/v1/advise | python3 -m json.tool` — its top pick must match a ranking you compute BY HAND from /v1/usage at the same moment, and you must paste both. Then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ in a browser and confirm the card names the same winner as the endpoint, with a clean console.

HARDWARE STEP IS FELIPE'S. Build with `make fw-build`, never flash. Append `FLASH REQUEST: sha=<short sha> reason=96 adds the use-this-next overlay on BtnA hold — owner action required` to progress.txt and MOVE ON. When he does authorise a release it goes through `sh scripts/release.sh`, which publishes a MERGED image — publishing .pio/build/<env>/firmware.bin bricked a stick on 2026-09-08 with 'Invalid image block, can't boot'.
